ios.desc:
Meet TimerVana — The Smarter Way to Orchestrate Your Time 
There are dozens of timer apps out there — stopwatches, countdowns, interval timers, Pomodoro clocks. But each focuses on one thing at a time and often ends the moment your phone locks or you switch apps. With TimerVana, you’re not just setting a timer — you’re designing a flow, a sequence of steps, a guided timer story that powers cooking, training, studying, routines, and more.
Why TimerVana is different
	•	Sequence-first design. Instead of a single timer, TimerVana lets you build step-by-step workflows: e.g. “Preheat → Chop → Cook → Rest → Serve” for a recipe, or “Warm-up → Work → Rest → Repeat” for a HIIT session. Each step lives within the same session and knows its place in the whole.
	•	Local-first, privacy-respecting. Your timers, your data. Unless you choose to share, everything runs on your device. No hidden uploads. No surprise tracking.
	•	Background and locked-screen reliability. Many timers pause or mute when your screen turns off or you switch apps. TimerVana takes advantage of iOS 26+ AlarmKit (on supported devices) so that even if your phone is locked, your alerts still sound. On older devices we fall back to local notifications—so you stay notified.
	•	Share and discover. The built-in community site (timervana.net) gives your workflows a second life. Publish your favorite timer sequences, browse what others have built (workouts, recipes, study routines, ADHD-friendly timers) and import them in one tap. Sharing isn’t an afterthought—it’s built in.
	•	Simple to use, powerful to build. Yes it’s easy enough to set up a 3-step timer in minutes. But if you want to build multi-hour routines, pin an end time, or build timed dependencies (e.g., start Step 3 only after Step 1 completes and Step 2 runs concurrently) — TimerVana has you covered.
What you can do with TimerVana
	•	Create sequential timers for everything: cooking, performances, workouts, study blocks, routines, rituals.
	•	Stay informed anywhere: voice announcements, local notifications, and if your device supports it, AlarmKit alerts that fire even when your phone is locked or idle.
	•	Track progress: Monitor remaining time, see which step is running or next, and get visual feedback on total session completion.
	•	Share or discover: Upload your own timer sequences, browse community creations, import with one tap into your library.

quotes.text:
Hi HN, I’m the creator of TimerVana.

It's not just "another timer app".  The engineering analogy is a lightweight task scheduler for things people do in the real world. A normal timer models one countdown. TimerVana models a small dependency graph in JSON: some steps run sequentially, others run in parallel, and everything can converge on a target finish time. You can also combine multiple timers (e.g., combine a timer with all the steps to cook a steak + a timer for roasting vegetables).

I originally built it because I often set multiple timers and alarms when cooking and got tired of repeatedly juggling separate alarms to get a main dish and several sides ready together. The same model also works for workouts, study sessions, morning routines, and other repeatable processes.

The iPhone app is local-first by design [0]. You can create, save, and run timers entirely on your phone without an account or cloud sharing. If you want the networked features, the companion website lets you browse and download timers, upload your own, and share them with other people.

Everything available today is free. I may eventually add optional AI-assisted timer creation as a paid feature, but I haven’t settled on the business model or pricing. I'm more doing this to solve my own problem and hope it will help others as well.
